clue.text: 8's more likely to break — some might say bust — a US server

indicators.note: 8 across is the don famous for swapping the opening sounds of word pairs, so this phrase is to be said his way

parts.words: more likely to break — some might say bust
parts.note: frailer is more likely to break; tits is a crude word for a bust, hence 'some might say'

explanation.surface: A tennis serve that is liable to break, put in a deliberately coarse way.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the opening sounds of FRAILER TITS and you hear TAYLOR FRITZ. 'Break' and 'server' play on tennis, where a server's game can be broken.
explanation.definitionFit: Taylor Fritz is an American professional tennis player, and every player takes turns serving in a match.

clue.text: Post-operative bottles one drinks?

indicators.note: to bottle is to hold inside, so the opening words contain what is wanted

parts.note: sitting across the join of the hyphenated word

explanation.surface: A patient fresh from surgery sneaking a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs from the end of 'Post' into 'operative'.
explanation.definitionFit: A toper is a habitual heavy drinker, literally a person who drinks.

clue.text: You end a riot? Capital!

indicators.note: a riot is disorder, so the preceding words are thrown into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone cheering a person who brings a riot to an end: capital work!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital!' looks like old-fashioned praise; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Yaoundé is the city that serves as the seat of government of Cameroon in central Africa.

clue.text: Missed alarm as a result of those faced by 9 and 24/26 — permit to include its first

parts.note: 9 and 24/26 are cricketers, and a batter faces deliveries in sets of six

indicators.note: to include something is to take it in, so one piece is placed within another

parts.note: to permit is to let

indicators.note: its refers back to the word permit, and first asks for that word's opening letter only

parts.note: the opening letter of this word

explanation.surface: Cricketers missing an early alarm call because of the bowling they must face.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled at the batters, so it is what a batter faces. 'Its first' means the first letter of permit.
explanation.definitionFit: To have overslept is to have stayed asleep past the intended waking time, sleeping through the clock's ringing.

clue.text: Companion to Donner und Blitzen can upset in the German

indicators.note: in places the jumbled letters within the next piece

parts.note: der is a German word for the

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, so the letters of the word before are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Something in German upsetting the reindeer team, with 'und' lending the phrase a Germanic air.
explanation.walkthrough: Donner and Blitzen are two of Santa's reindeer; the German 'und' hints that the article should also be German.
explanation.definitionFit: Dancer is another of Santa's reindeer, named alongside Donner and Blitzen in the traditional list.

clue.text: Have nothing to do with nothing in returning prima donna

indicators.note: returning means coming back, so the following word is read from right to left
in puts the first piece inside the turned-round word

parts.note: a prima donna is a diva
the round zero shape

explanation.surface: Shunning a temperamental star singer who has come back to the company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nothing' appears twice: once in the definition phrase, once as the zero letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To avoid someone is to keep away from them and refuse any dealings, the same as having nothing to do with them.

clue.text: Buffalo Bill back before a boar shot

indicators.note: back signals reading the abbreviation in the opposite direction

parts.note: AC, short for account, is a bill

indicators.note: shot means ruined or wrecked, so the letters before it are broken up and reordered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Buffalo Bill, the Wild West showman, backing away before shooting a boar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buffalo Bill' reads as one name, but it splits: Buffalo is the definition and Bill begins the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The carabao is the domesticated water buffalo of the Philippines, used for ploughing.

clue.text: Crowd's customary welcome for 9 includes seedy motel vacancy

indicators.note: includes means the first piece wraps round the jumbled one

parts.note: fans greet the batter 9 across by booming his surname

indicators.note: seedy means run-down and disreputable, so the word after it is messed about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A cricket crowd's chant for its hero, and a shabby motel with a spare room.
explanation.walkthrough: England crowds greet Joe Root with a long drawn-out 'Rooooot' that sounds like booing. The jumbled motel goes inside after ROO.
explanation.definitionFit: A room to let is accommodation available for rent, the sign a landlord shows when there is space free.

clue.text: Oxford don who likes a post-coital cuddle

definitions.meaning: first meaning: William ..., warden of New College, Oxford, famed for transposing sounds
second meaning: one who spoons, lying nestled close behind a partner

explanation.walkthrough: The surface pins an indiscretion on a single don; the clue is really two meanings of one name.
explanation.definitionFit: Spooner is the surname of the Oxford academic, and spooning is the close curled embrace, so a spooner is one who enjoys it.

clue.text: 8's eggs and fibre in batter

indicators.note: 8 across is the don known for swapping opening sounds, so the phrase that follows is spoken his way

parts.note: roe is fish eggs; jute is a coarse plant fibre

explanation.surface: A recipe: eggs and fibre stirred into a batter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Batter' looks like the cooking mixture; it is a cricketer. Swap the opening sounds of ROE JUTE.
explanation.definitionFit: Joe Root is an England cricketer and one of the leading run-scorers in Test history, a batter by role.

clue.text: 8's judicious bet on England 9

indicators.note: 8 across is the don known for swapping opening sounds, so the next phrase is spoken his way

parts.note: canny is shrewd or judicious; a dare is a challenge or wager

explanation.surface: A shrewd wager placed on England's number 9.
explanation.walkthrough: With 9 across a cricketer, 'England 9' seems to point there; it means the rugby shirt number 9, the scrum-half.
explanation.definitionFit: Danny Care played scrum-half for England's rugby union side, the position that wears shirt number nine.

clue.text: Thousands and thousands initially inside place where 1/21, 9, 10, 12/20 and 24/26 might be seen

definitions.text: place where 1/21, 9, 10, 12/20 and 24/26 might be seen

indicators.note: inside places the selected letter within the phrase before it

parts.note: a grand is a thousand pounds or dollars
taken as written

indicators.note: initially points to the starting letter of the word just before it

parts.note: the opening letter of this word

explanation.surface: Spectators by the thousand packed into a stadium to watch the sporting stars of the puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: A grand is slang for a thousand pounds or dollars. The letter goes between the two words, not inside either one.
explanation.definitionFit: A grandstand is the main covered seating at a sports ground, where spectators watch the tennis, cricket, rugby and football players named.

clue.text: Scorer seen in 8's crystal ball

indicators.note: 8 across is the don known for swapping opening sounds, so the phrase after it is spoken his way

parts.note: crystal is slang for the drug crystal meth; a bead is a small ball

explanation.surface: A fortune-teller glimpsing a future goal-scorer in a crystal ball.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crystal ball' reads as one fortune-telling object; split it into two words and swap their opening sounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Beth Mead is an England women's footballer who finished as top goalscorer at Euro 2022.

clue.text: Note reverberated within?

indicators.note: something that reverberates bounces back, so the run of letters is read backwards
within says the letters lie inside the long word before it

parts.note: the run of letters after its first two

explanation.surface: A musical note echoing round the inside of a hall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reverberated' is both the word holding the letters and the signal that they come back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: A breve is a long musical note, equal in length to two semibreves.

clue.text: The faithful repudiate abridged Bible extract

indicators.note: abridged means shortened, so the last letter of the following word is cut

parts.note: to belie is to contradict or show to be false
a verse is a numbered passage of scripture

explanation.surface: Church members rejecting a passage cut from scripture.
explanation.definitionFit: Those of faith are people who hold a religious creed, so 'the faithful' collectively are its believers.

clue.text: Conquered lands and advanced with old leaders of resistance losing dogfight

parts.note: advanced in the sense of modern or up to date
W is the abbreviation for with
O is the abbreviation for old

indicators.note: leaders are those at the front, so only the opening letters of the next three words are taken

parts.note: the heads of these three words

explanation.surface: A wartime tale: territory taken, then the resistance fighters lose an air battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Losing' reads as an instruction to remove something, but it is simply a word whose first letter is wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: The New World is the Americas, seized and colonised by European powers after 1492.

clue.text: Plant's advice on how to make Britton grow?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an aquatic fern-like plant

definitions.text: advice on how to make Britton grow
definitions.meaning: second meaning: Fern Britton is a British television presenter, and plants need watering to grow

explanation.surface: Gardening tips on making a TV presenter grow, as if she were a houseplant.
explanation.walkthrough: Fern Britton is a well-known British daytime TV presenter; read as an instruction, the answer tells you to water her.
explanation.definitionFit: Water ferns are small floating aquatic ferns such as Azolla, found on ponds and ditches.

clue.text: Condensed e.g. copyright's length first, and reduced credit

indicators.note: reduced means made smaller, so the final letter of the next word is dropped
first asks for the measure to be placed ahead of the property item

parts.note: an ell is an old measure of cloth length
copyright is an example of intellectual property
tick is British slang for credit, as in buying on tick

explanation.surface: Legal shorthand about how long copyright lasts and a cut in credit.
explanation.walkthrough: To buy on tick is British for buying on credit.
explanation.definitionFit: Elliptic writing leaves words out, as in an ellipsis, so it is compressed or terse.

clue.text: Baby eluding changing

indicators.note: changing means altering, so the letters of the word before it are put in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An infant wriggling away from a nappy change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Baby' looks like a noun about an infant; it is the verb meaning to pamper.
explanation.definitionFit: To baby someone is to pamper them and give in to their wishes, which is to spoil or gratify them.

clue.text: 'Principle' is anyway alien to X

indicators.note: anyway here means in either direction, so the word reads the same forwards and backwards

parts.note: X is ten in Roman numerals
ET is the film alien

explanation.surface: A complaint that principles are foreign to X, the social media platform.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue says 'alien to X' but the pieces join with X first. Tenet is also the title of a film about time running backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenet is a principle or belief held as true by a group or person.

clue.text: Worry about Facebook owner's identity tracker

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first word is wrapped round the second

parts.note: to nag is to worry or pester
Meta is the company that owns Facebook

explanation.surface: Fretting about Facebook's parent company tracking people's identities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Identity tracker' sounds like online surveillance; it is a humble badge.
explanation.definitionFit: A name tag is a badge pinned to clothing that shows who someone is, so it keeps track of identities at events.

clue.text: See 12
Smoked, having first of rations cut, made ready for winter

indicators.note: having means holding, so the first word takes the other pieces inside it

parts.note: fumed oak is darkened by smoke-like ammonia fumes; to fume is to smoke

indicators.note: first of picks out the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: the opening letter of this word
to trim is to cut

explanation.surface: Food smoked, with rations reduced, to prepare for winter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' reads as an instruction to shorten rations, but it is the second word inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A coat edged with fur at collar and cuffs has been prepared to keep out the cold of the season.

clue.text: See 1 Across
A special occasion for an online rant?

parts.note: e- is the prefix for electronic, as in email
to vent is to let off steam, to rant

explanation.surface: Someone treating a good rant on the internet as a big occasion.
explanation.definitionFit: An event is a notable happening or organised function, the kind of thing marked as a special occasion.

clue.text: Announce withdrawal of lawsuit?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to speak out rhetorically
second meaning, whimsical: de- means removal and a claim is a legal action

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags an invented sense: read the answer as DE plus CLAIM, the undoing of a claim.
explanation.definitionFit: To declaim is to deliver a speech loudly and dramatically, so it means to proclaim or pronounce.

clue.text: Skipper below her best, according to 8

indicators.note: 8 across is the don known for swapping opening sounds, so the phrase is to be spoken as he would say it

parts.note: nether means lower; a height is a peak or best

explanation.surface: A captain playing below her best form.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the opening sounds of NETHER HEIGHT. 'Skipper' seems a sailor, but means team captain.
explanation.definitionFit: Heather Knight captained the England women's cricket team, and skipper is the usual sports term for a captain.

clue.text: Conduct unbecoming when Carlisle gets together with a zealot

indicators.note: getting together means joining up, so the pieces are run into one word

parts.note: the tail end of the city name
taken as written
the opening pair of letters

explanation.surface: Scandalous behaviour when a Carlisle man teams up with a fanatic.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer lies across Carlisle, a and zealot once they are joined, with the words between skipped; Carlisle is a city in Cumbria in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleaze is sordid or corrupt behaviour, the kind of improper conduct expected to disgrace public figures.
